_comment: FIXTURE CORPUS - NOT THE REAL KNOWLEDGE BASE.
Fourteen short passages standing in for pages on the domains CONNECT Plus
treats as trusted. The wording here is paraphrased guidance written for this
fixture, not text copied from those sites, and the URLs are illustrative.
Purpose: let stages 07-09 and the eval harness run before connectplus-rag
has crawled anything. Replace with real retrieval, do not extend this to
Coverage is deliberately incomplete. There is nothing here about medical
advice, visas or immigration, or which phone to buy, because the eval set
asks those questions and the correct behaviour is to refuse them.

chunks.title: Text message scams
chunks.text: Scammers send text messages that look like they come from a bank, a delivery company or a government agency. The message usually asks you to click a link or call a number urgently. Do not click links in text messages you did not expect. Do not call the number in the message. If you are worried the message might be real, find the organisation's phone number yourself and call that instead. Delete the message once you have checked.

chunks.title: Report a scam
chunks.text: You can report a scam to Scamwatch online. Reporting helps warn other people even if you did not lose any money. Take a screenshot of the message before you delete it. If you gave away bank details or clicked a link and entered information, contact your bank straight away. Your bank can stop payments and watch your account.

chunks.title: Prize and lottery scams
chunks.text: A message saying you have won a prize, a lottery or a gift card is almost always a scam, especially if you did not enter a competition. Real prizes never ask you to pay a fee or give bank details to collect them. Do not reply to the message and do not send money. Block the sender and delete the message.

chunks.title: Problems signing in to myGov
chunks.text: If you cannot sign in to myGov, check that you are using the username or email address you signed up with. Use the Forgot password link on the sign in page to set a new password. myGov will send a code to your mobile phone or email to confirm it is you. If you no longer have that phone number, you will need to call the myGov helpdesk to update it.

chunks.title: Sign in security and codes
chunks.text: myGov asks for a security code as well as your password. This is called two-factor authentication. It means someone who steals your password still cannot get into your account. The code is sent by text message to the mobile number saved on your account, or generated by the myGov app. The code lasts only a few minutes. myGov will never phone you and ask you to read a code out loud. Anyone who does that is a scammer.

chunks.title: Express Plus Medicare mobile app
chunks.text: The Express Plus Medicare app lets you claim a Medicare rebate, view your Medicare card and update your bank details from your phone. Download it free from the App Store or Google Play. You sign in with your myGov details the first time, then you can set a four digit PIN for later. Claims usually arrive in your bank account within a few days.

chunks.title: Centrelink phone self service
chunks.text: You can use Centrelink phone self service to report income, check payments and make a claim without going to a service centre. You will need your Customer Reference Number and your phone self service PIN. If you do not have a PIN, staff can set one up for you. Free interpreters are available on the phone if you ask.

chunks.title: Staying safe online for seniors
chunks.text: Use a different password for your bank, your email and myGov. A long password made of three or four unrelated words is easier to remember and harder to guess. Never give a password or a security code to anyone who contacts you, even if they say they are from your bank or the government. Real organisations do not ask for those.

chunks.title: Making a video call
chunks.text: Video calling apps such as Messenger, Viber, Zalo and WhatsApp let you see family overseas at no cost beyond your internet. Connect to Wi-Fi first so the call does not use your mobile data. Open the app, find the person in your contact list, and tap the video camera icon. If the picture freezes, hang up and call again on Wi-Fi.

chunks.title: Be Connected free digital skills
chunks.text: Be Connected is a free Australian Government programme that helps older people build digital skills. It has step by step online courses and a network of community centres where a person can sit with you and show you on your own device. Some centres run sessions in languages other than English. There is a free phone helpline for older Australians who need help getting started.

chunks.title: TIS National free interpreting
chunks.text: TIS National provides interpreters for people who do not speak English fluently. The service is free when you contact most Australian government agencies. Call 131 450 and ask for a Vietnamese interpreter, then give the interpreter the name and number of the agency you want to reach. Doctors and many community services can also book an interpreter for you at no cost.

chunks.title: Blocking scam calls and messages
chunks.text: You can block a number on your phone so it cannot call or message you again. On most phones, open the message or recent call, tap the sender's number, then choose Block. You can also report scam calls and texts by forwarding the message to 7226, which spells SCAM on a phone keypad. Blocking one number does not stop all scams, because scammers change numbers often.

chunks.title: When your phone runs slowly
chunks.text: A phone often slows down when its storage is nearly full or when apps have not been updated. Delete photos and videos you have already saved somewhere else. Remove apps you do not use. Check for updates in the App Store or Google Play and install them. Restarting the phone once a week also helps.

chunks.title: Using Wi-Fi instead of mobile data
chunks.text: Mobile data is the internet your phone uses when it is not on Wi-Fi, and it is limited by your plan. Wi-Fi at home does not count towards that limit. Open Settings, tap Wi-Fi, choose your home network and enter the password once. The phone will connect by itself after that. Watching videos uses far more data than messages or email.
